goodbye.note: Also very common: Hasta luego. Casual in Latin America: Chao.

thank_you.note: Thank you very much: Muchas gracias.

youre_welcome.note: Also: No hay de qué. In parts of Latin America (e.g. Colombia) you will often hear Con gusto.

yes.note: Keep the accent: si without it means 'if'.

no.note: Same spelling as English, but a short, pure 'o' with no glide.

sorry.note: For a small slip, like bumping into someone: Perdón.

excuse_me.note: Also: Perdone. To a friend (tú): Disculpa.

good_morning.note: Used until lunchtime, which in Spain can be 2 p.m.

how_are_you.note: Usted is often dropped: ¿Cómo está? To a friend: ¿Cómo estás? or ¿Qué tal?

im_fine.note: Fuller: Estoy bien, gracias. Ask back with ¿Y usted?

whats_your_name.note: To a friend or child: ¿Cómo te llamas?

my_name_is.note: Also: Mi nombre es …, which sounds a little more formal.

nice_to_meet_you.note: Also: Encantado; a woman says Encantada.

im_from.note: Uses ser, not estar, because origin is permanent.

speak_slowly.note: Short version: Más despacio, por favor.

what.note: To ask someone to repeat, ¿Cómo? sounds more polite.

why.note: Two words with an accent. Porque (one word) means 'because'.

who.note: Asking about more than one person: ¿Quiénes?

how_much.note: Often just ¿Cuánto cuesta? When paying the total: ¿Cuánto es?

where_bathroom.note: In Spain also: ¿Dónde están los servicios? or ¿Dónde está el aseo?

can_you_help.note: Also: ¿Puede ayudarme? To a friend: ¿Me ayudas?

what_time.note: In parts of Latin America also: ¿Qué horas son?

one.note: Before a masculine noun it becomes un (un café); feminine: una.

five.note: In most of Spain the first c sounds like English 'th'; in Latin America like 's'.

water.note: Feminine, but takes el: el agua. Still water: agua sin gas.

tea.note: The accent tells it apart from te ('you').

menu_please.note: Latin America: El menú, por favor. In Spain, el menú often means the set lunch.

no_meat.note: Also: Soy vegetariano; a woman says Soy vegetariana.

left.note: Turn left: Gire a la izquierda.

right.note: Don't mix it up with derecho, which means 'straight on' in Latin America.

straight_ahead.note: In Latin America: Derecho or Todo derecho.

stop_here.note: Also common: Déjeme aquí, por favor.

hotel.note: Same spelling as English, but the h is silent: 'o-TEL'.

want_to_go.note: Softer: Quisiera ir a … Before el, a + el becomes al (al centro).

is_it_far.note: The answer you hope for: Está cerca ('it's close').

one_ticket.note: In Latin America: Un boleto, por favor (in some countries, un pasaje).

too_expensive.note: For a feminine noun: demasiado cara. Casual: ¡Qué caro!

id_like_this.note: When buying, also very common: Me llevo esto.

just_looking.note: In Latin America also: Solo estoy viendo, gracias.

cash.note: Cash as a noun: el efectivo.

big.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

small.note: Feminine: pequeña. In much of Latin America also: chico / chica.

today.note: The h is silent: sounds like 'oy'.

now.note: Right now: ahora mismo. In Mexico, ahorita can mean 'now' or 'in a little while'.

good_evening.note: Used from lunch until dark. After dark the greeting is Buenas noches.

good_night.note: Also the greeting after dark. Before bed you can add: Que descanse.

wait_moment.note: Fuller: Espere un momento, por favor.

call_police.note: To a friend (tú): ¡Llama a la policía!

need_doctor.note: In Latin America also: Necesito un doctor.

dont_feel_well.note: In Spain also: Me encuentro mal.

hospital.note: Same spelling as English, but the h is silent and the stress is on the end: os-pee-TAL.

lost_phone.note: Spain: He perdido el móvil. Latin America: Perdí mi celular.

allergic.note: A woman says: Soy alérgica a …

be_careful.note: As a quick warning shout: ¡Cuidado! To a friend: ¡Ten cuidado!

of_course.note: In everyday talk, ¡Claro! is even more common.

maybe.note: Also: tal vez. In casual speech, in Spain and Latin America alike: a lo mejor.

dont_know.note: Keep the accent: se without it is a different word.

im_happy.note: A woman says: Estoy contenta. Also common: Estoy feliz (same for both).

welcome.note: To a woman: ¡Bienvenida! To a group: ¡Bienvenidos!
